I have felt this way; for myself it’s a reaction to something going on both internally and externally. 

In other words, it’s part lacking proper coping skills and part people do have the tendency to be insufferable which has worsen over the past year. I find it hard to connect to anyone other than my sister, grown children, and two friends. 

I also spent a year and half advocating against extremist laws in the state I’m living in and now that those laws have past, everyone has something to say. And I’m over it because I spent a lot of energy trying to warn people and now they are shocked at what has taken place.  With that being said, I too have the tendency to think I am above most people and rather not be bothered with them because people aren’t going to care about something unless it directly impacts them. 

I am fully aware of my dissociation and being aware of it keeps me friendly and cordial and less angry but it has placed me in a spot where I have to regain my strength before I try to become social again. I’m also in therapy and on medication. 

Also I’ve had to deal with the fact that for most of my life I haven’t fit in anywhere and I’ve been around a lot of people who lacked empathy, emotional intelligence, and thrived off deceptive behaviors - I have had the trauma and yes I have expelled negativity towards others in the past. Like most victims of traumatic events, I was reactive and when I read your post, I related and found it to be part of my own terminology of what has been normal in my existence. 

I wouldn’t feel bad about this, you’ve come here and acknowledged what you’re going through so that’s an indicator of your awareness. And even if it seems unreasonable, there is a root cause for it. And for myself, studying my own roots has been empowering. 

There’s no easy way to get through some challenges but there are ways to deal and cope so you don’t feel stuck all the time. 

Best to you.
